title: fix(vscode-extension): provide folding ranges for templates with inte…
body:
Inline templates written as template literals with `${...}` substitutions are `TemplateExpression` nodes, not string literals, so they were not recognized when building the virtual HTML document. The HTML language service received a blank document and produced no folding ranges, breaking element folding for the whole template.

Match template expressions in addition to string-literal-like nodes and blank out the `${...}` substitutions (preserving line breaks) so offsets in the virtual document stay aligned and the expression contents are not parsed as HTML.

Fixes #65508

## What is the current behavior?

When an inline template is written as a template literal containing a `${...}` substitution, folding ranges for the elements in the template are lost. The language server does not recognize the template (a `TemplateExpression` is not a string-literal-like node), so the virtual HTML document used for folding is blank and the HTML language service returns no ranges. In the editor, the folding arrows for the template's elements disappear (VS Code may partially mask this with indentation-based folding when the template is cleanly indented).

Issue Number: #65508

## What is the new behavior?

Template literals with `${...}` substitutions are now matched when building the virtual HTML document. The substitution expressions are blanked out (preserving line breaks) so document offsets stay aligned and the expression contents are not parsed as HTML. Folding ranges are produced for all elements of the template, exactly as for templates without substitutions.

- [ ] Yes
